3B) A thin cylindrical shell is 3.5m long and 1.2m in internal diameter. It is subjected to (2)  
internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. If the thickness of the sheet is 10mm, find the  
circumferential stress and longitudinal stress. Take E=200 GPa and p= 0.3.

3C)             A rectangular bar of 300mm length is 100 mm wide and 30mm thick. It is loaded with  
  an axial tensile load of 200 kN, together with a normal compressive force of 500kN on  
  the face 100mm x 300 mm and a tensile force 400 kN on the face 30mm x 300mm.  
  Calculate the Poisson's ratio, strain in all the three directions if the change in volume is  
  195.408 mm3 and also find the change in dimension in the direction of 500 kN load.  
  $$Take E = 200 GPa.$$  
  (5)  
  
  
4A)             i) Derive the relationship between Young's modulus (E) and Bulk modulus (K).  
  ii) Explain the state of simple shear stress.                                                  (5)  
  
4B)             A bar made up of three different materials is shown in figure. All segments of the bar are  
  of 10 mm thickness and subjected to axial loads as indicated. Determine the stresses  
  developed in the segments AB and BC and the stresses developed at the ends of the  
  tapered bar. Also determine the total deformation of the bar. Consider Eal = 70 GPa, Est  
  $$= 210 GPa and Ebr = 100 GPa.$$  
  
  
  (5)  
  
  
5A)             A steel hollow tube of internal diameter 50mm and thickness 10mm has a solid rod of  
  copper of diameter 50mm placed snuggly inside it. The compound bar thus formed is  
  rigidly joined at their contact surfaces at a temperature of 20° C. Determine the stresses  
  in steel and copper if the temperature is raised to 40° C. Take Esteel = 200GPa and        (5)  
  Ecopper = 100GPa. Also, temperature expansion coefficient of steel and copper are 1x  
  10-6/ ° C and 1.5x10-6/ ° C respectively.  
  
5B)             A hollow steel pipe of internal diameter 100mm is filled with concrete inside. What  
  must be the thickness of the steel pipe required such that under the action of axial force (3)  
  P, both steel and concrete will carry equal load ? Esteel = 200GPa and Econcrete = 30GPa.  
  
5C)             Explain temperature stress with an example.
